title: The Premature Decay of the Wicked
english: Having achieved nothing, its cutting will be destroyed before its time. For this reason its flower falls and its shoot withers, because it does not remain for the time of perfect fruit. This is similar to the saying, 'Do not become hardened, so that you do not die before your time.'me.'me.' Some, being disturbed by such words, propose fate and say, 'we are under the time in which we act.' But 'before the time' refers to 'before the bringing to completion,' just as we say a time is early or late.

Thus indeed Job says that he 'has come into a tomb like grain ripe, being gathered according to the season' (Job 29:17). And it is a blessing of God that the shoot is destroyed by wickedness before its time. And its rose will not thicken; it might be as early as an eye, and it would fall like the flower of an olive... Its flower is not permitted to come to a perfect fruit-bearing. And nothing less than this, as it is foretold, is effective and useful; it is a sign of the wickedness present in those who act.

But for the righteous it is not so; for the branches of the true vine, remaining in their nature, grow and bear fruit. For the death of the impious is a testimony. After passing through what perishes, the end appears as the death of the impious. For the working of wickedness achieves death, not the common death, but the death of punishment. And fire will burn the houses of the bribe-takers.

And according to immediate benefit it has utility, because the bribe-takers certainly undergo this upon injustices and impieties. For it has been said: 'The ruler asks, and the judge spoke peaceful words; it is the incense of his soul' (Proverbs 17:8). How then the house of the bribe-taker burns, it must be understood. It has been said: 'And I will take away their good things like a shepherd turning away and walking according to a rule in a day of scrutiny.' For in the examination of things there will be a repayment according to what is said: 'Go into the eternal fire' (Matthew 25:41). There is a time even in this life when the repayment begins...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Judgment and the Deceit of the Belly
english: Judgment will come against the gifted. Because 'the judgment of God is present' (Rom 2:5), those who pervert the judgments of God fall under punishments. And in the belly, pains shall be taken. He means this: the man becomes a father of ill-born ones, being the cause of punishments.

However, the divine rewards are not produced by man, but God grants them; 'for the sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be revealed to us with the coming glory' (Rom 8:18).:18).:18). We don't mean to say that the diligent one is not the cause of good things, but that the graces of God and the gifts are provided through incomparable excellence from him; 'for every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights' (Jas 1:17).

Because for the wicked, the manner of punishment follows, they themselves bringing it upon themselves, but to the diligent, God directs the graces, it has been said: 'those I will glorify, but those dishonoring me shall be dishonored' (Heb 2:6). Because the dishonoring of God brings upon them dishonor. Paul also writes: 'To those who seek glory and honor through t good work, God gives eternal life' (Rom 2:7), but 'to those from selfish ambition and who disobey the truth, wrath and anger' (Romans 2:8) follow.

It will depart from him empty, and his belly will be filled with deceit. All his efforts, as it is foretold, are filled with futility, iving pains in the belly. conceived toil and brought forth injustice' (Job 15:16), making it clear that his belly carries deceit. And deceit here he says is all manner of wickedness.

For deceit is indeed a kind of wickedness, and nothing less, and all wickedness is called by the name according to what has been said: 'O full of all deceit and all trickery' (Matt 23:28) and 'therefore laying aside all deceit and hypocrisy' (1 Pet 2:22). However, the belly refers to [the seat of the soul/desire], and it sympathizes with the evil or with the good. Having understood, Job says: I have heard such things.

title: The Nature of Job's Friends' Counsel
english: There are many accusers of evils. By doing so, they show that, having been with men, he has heard  much.nd since they bring their accusations to those in distress without distinction, as if to separate them as bad ones, it is appropriate—just as the three friends have done—that he brought the phrase 'all are accusers of evils,' meaning that all, through ignorance of what is happening differently than it ought, either raise up or contract the painful things; or he said 'all' regarding the three, for from this number comes the multitude. What's the point? Is not the arrangement of words a matter of the spirit? spirit? spirit? [Gap] exhortation.' Even if others, suffering and lamenting, are satisfied with their own lamentations, by this the salvation of friends is to be preferred. Job 16:6b: 'And if I keep silent, how much less shall I be wounded?' 'And if indeed in silence,' he says, 'I were to contain the insults, I would not only fail to attain the glory of philosophy, but on the contrary, I would be judged much more unlawfully for the silence of one thought to be conscious of the things being said.' He had not previously done this, but it happened because the adversary requested it. 'Foolish' here means the insensitivity; for 'having struck' is joined to this.
